title: Exclusive Running Time of Functions

concept.title: The call stack: the running function is on top
body: Functions call other functions, and a program keeps track of this with a **call stack**: the function that is running is on the top. The log tells when a function **starts** or **ends** (`id:start:time` or `id:end:time`; an end at time `t` includes the whole time unit `t`). You want, for every function, its **exclusive time**: the time it ran itself, without the time of the functions it called.

Keep the stack of running function ids and the time `prev` from which the top function runs undisturbed. When a function **starts** at `t`: the function on top (if any) ran from `prev` to `t`, so add `t - prev` to it; push the new one; `prev = t`. When a function **ends** at `t`: it ran from `prev` to the end of `t`, so add `t - prev + 1`; pop it; `prev = t + 1`.
The `+ 1` at the end and `prev = t + 1` come from the rule that the end time is inclusive: a function that starts at 0 and ends at 0 ran for one unit.

statement: A single thread runs `n` functions with ids `0` to `n - 1`. A function can call other functions, and the call can be nested. You get a log of `m` lines in the form `id:start:time` or `id:end:time` in order of time. A function ends at the **end** of the time unit `time` (so a function that starts and ends at the same time unit ran for 1 unit). The exclusive time of a function is the time it ran, not counting the time of the functions it called. Print the exclusive time of every function.
inputFormat: The second line has the `m` log entries.
outputFormat: Print `n` numbers: the exclusive time of function 0, 1, ..., n - 1.
constraints: The log is valid: every start has a matching end, calls are nested, and the time never goes back (after an end at time `t`, the next event has a time of at least `t + 1`).

examples.note: Function 1 ran during 2..5 = 4 units. Function 0 ran during 0..1 and 6..6 = 3 units.

hints: Keep a stack of function ids and the time `prev` from which the top function runs.
On a start, charge the time since `prev` to the function below, then push.
On an end, charge `t - prev + 1` to the function and set `prev = t + 1`.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
logs = input().split()

# Your code here

explanation: A stack holds the running functions. Each event charges the time since `prev` to the function that was running, and `prev` moves on, with the inclusive end time handled by the `+ 1`.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
logs = input().split()

time = [0] * n
stack = []
prev = 0
for entry in logs:
    fid, kind, t = entry.split(":")
    fid = int(fid)
    t = int(t)
    if kind == "start":
        if stack:
            time[stack[-1]] += t - prev
        stack.append(fid)
        prev = t
    else:
        time[stack.pop()] += t - prev + 1
        prev = t + 1
print(*time)
